sources.entry: How to improve your Docker containers security

summary.title: Docker Security Best Practices Cheat Sheet for Secure Containers
summary.one_liner: You learn a practical checklist of Docker container hardening measures covering images, runtime flags, filesystem and network isolation, vulnerability scanning, secrets, and registry security.
takeaways: Run containers as a non-root user, avoid privileged mode, and use --security-opt=no-new-privileges.
Drop unneeded Linux capabilities and limit CPU and memory with cgroups.
Do not expose /var/run/docker.sock or sensitive host mounts; use custom bridge networks instead of docker0.
Scan base images, dependencies and CI/CD builds with tools like Trivy or Snyk, and keep secrets out of images and Dockerfiles.
Secure registries with RBAC, image signing via Docker Content Trust, and TLS.
summary.summary: The article walks through Docker security fundamentals and then a set of best practices grouped into image security, container runtime, host filesystem, network, vulnerability scanning, secrets management, and registry supply chain protection. Each section gives short explanations and command-line examples such as docker run flags for memory and CPU limits, read-only tmpfs mounts, and trivy severity-based exit codes. It closes with common pitfalls and an FAQ. The page is partly promotional, pushing GitGuardian's ggshield secret scanner and a cheat sheet download.
